subject: SIG: SDLC artifact follow-up — PR gating & ephemeral secrets proofs
messages:
From: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@kitecompliance.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG intake — SDLC artifacts: PR gating, CI controls, secrets rotation

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Horizon Payments' SIG intake, we need a short set of artifacts that demonstrate your secure SDLC controls for code review, CI gating, and secrets management. Specifically we're looking for:

- A small sampling (2-3) of PR gating logs that show required reviewers, branch protection enforcement, and automated checks blocking merges. Redact usernames if needed.
- Evidence of ephemeral credential usage and rotation for CI agents (screenshots or short log extracts showing token creation and expiry).
- CI access matrix or role mapping for pipeline runners and who can push changes to production branches.
- A brief narrative (1 paragraph) describing your formal change approval flow and emergency patch exceptions.

If possible, please provide these items by EOD Monday (2028-05-15). If you prefer to share a Drive folder link and a JIRA ticket referencing the artifacts, that's fine.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Carter
Senior Assessor, Kite Compliance
lisa.carter@kitecompliance.com

Irene — can you extract the ephemeral token sample / screenshot from the runner logs and include a one-paragraph change-control narrative. Let's aim to consolidate into a single Drive folder and attach in one reply. If anything will slip the date, call it out here.

Subject: Re: SIG intake — quick clarification on artifacts

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifications so we know the acceptance criteria:

1) For PR gating logs we need at least one example that shows the exact automated enforcement (i.e., a blocked merge followed by a green build and then merge). A short context line pointing to the log lines that show "merge blocked by branch protection" is helpful.
2) For ephemeral tokens: we need either a screenshot or a log snippet that shows token issuance with timestamp and expiry, and ideally a little narrative confirming token TTL and rotation policy.
3) CI access matrix looks good — can you add which JIRA role (group) corresponds to "prod-deployer"?

If you can add those items into a single Drive folder and drop the link here by EOD Friday (2028-05-16) we'll mark this intake as complete.

Thanks,
Lisa
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai

Lisa / Sean / Marissa — apologies for the slight delay. I've dropped a consolidated folder with the requested artifacts and added short annotations next to each file. Highlights below: 

- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSDLCArtifacts (folder contains three redacted samples and the narrative).
- sdlc-pr-gating-sample-logs-2028-04.txt: lines 44-66 show "merge blocked: branch protection" followed by CI retry and successful merge. Redaction: usernames replaced by roles.
- ephemeral-token-rollover-sample.png: screenshot from the ephemeral token service showing issuance at 2028-04-21T03:02:17Z and expiry at 2028-04-21T03:17:17Z (15m TTL). Log excerpt named token-issue-20280421.log is in the folder.
- ci-access-matrix-2028Q1.pdf: I've added a footnote mapping prod-deployer to the JIRA group "jira-prod-admins" and linked JIRA-INT-4821 for current membership.
- change-control narrative: short paragraph in README.txt describing PR review, owner approval, canary deploy gating, and emergency patch procedure (requires 2 approvers + incident manager review).

Attachments included as stubs in this thread: sdlc-pr-gating-sample-logs-2028-04.txt; ephemeral-token-rollover-sample.png; ci-access-matrix-2028Q1.pdf

Let me know if you need raw log lines (we can provide redacted extracts) or a short Zoom to walk the assessor through the Drive folder.

Thanks,
